solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Salvation Army taken in by more rough-and-ready evangelist?

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: cruder means more rough-and-ready

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army preacher is welcomed by an even rougher gospel enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as loose: a crusader campaigns zealously for a cause, as an evangelist does.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is a zealous campaigner, and an evangelist is someone who preaches a cause with missionary fervour.

clue.text: Energetic, like a team with ten players dismissed?

definitions.text: like a team with ten players dismissed?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in cricket a side is ... when ten of its eleven batsmen have been dismissed

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket innings ends when ten batsmen are out, since the last one has no partner: the team is then all out.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out effort is one using every bit of strength, which is what being energetic means here.

clue.text: Sailor is a knave

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., or ... Tar, is slang for a sailor
second meaning: the knave is the ... in a pack of playing cards

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to call a seaman a rogue; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Tar is a traditional nickname for a seaman, and the court card below the queen is called either knave or jack.

clue.text: Ambassador and a university lecturer face to face

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An envoy and an academic meet in a direct confrontation.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the title used for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-on meeting is a direct, frontal one, with the two parties confronting each other squarely.

clue.text: Times collection for a whole year?

definitions.text: Times collection for a whole year?

parts.words: Times collection for a whole year?
parts.note: read as a gathering of dates and days spanning twelve months, not a bound volume of The Times newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Times' look like the newspaper; it is simply the dates of the year collected in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar sets out all the days, weeks and months of one year in a single chart.

clue.text: Doughty-sounding old Labour leader

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for doughty is heard rather than spelt as it is

parts.note: doughty means hardy, tough and resolute

explanation.surface: A tough-sounding figure from the early Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Hardie was the founder and first leader of the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Keir Hardie, Scottish socialist, became the first parliamentary leader of the Labour Party in 1906.

clue.text: Thin film director

definitions.meaning: second meaning: David ... directed Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an insult to a skinny director; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim person is described as lean, and Sir David Lean was a celebrated British filmmaker.

clue.text: Information being published concerning property contract

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding, as in business letters
a lease is a contract letting property for a set term

explanation.surface: News is issued about a tenancy agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A release, such as a press release, is a statement of information issued to the public.

clue.text: Saw notice ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of places the notice before the word for time in the answer

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an announcement before the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past tense of see; here it is the noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, exactly what an adage is.

clue.text: Start to sample white wine in jar

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of sample

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Begin tasting the white wine kept in a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container for the wine, but it is a verb or noun meaning a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jar is a sudden jolt or unpleasant surprise, which is a shock.

clue.text: German city reds getting excited in small room?

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for a small room

parts.note: a den is a small private room or study

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the letters of reds are rearranged

explanation.surface: Political radicals get worked up in a cramped room in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reds' looks like communists in the scene, but it is just letters to be stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital of Saxony in eastern Germany, on the Elbe.

clue.text: Got off school in exploit

indicators.note: in places the word for school within the word for exploit

parts.note: an exploit is a deed, a notable act
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Someone escaped school by some daring feat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to teach or coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to alight from a railway carriage, so detrained means got off the train.

clue.text: Pursuing every possibility, despite expectations

parts.note: after means pursuing or in pursuit of
all means everything, every possibility

explanation.surface: Chasing every option, contrary to what was expected.
explanation.definitionFit: After all is an idiom meaning in spite of what had been thought or anticipated.

clue.text: Some feel magic in this wood

indicators.note: some of the phrase means only part of its letters are used, sitting inside the words

explanation.surface: People sense something magical among these trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is the timber of the elm tree, a hardwood used in furniture.

clue.text: Created about awful rain — it's wet in the kitchen!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for created goes round the other letters

parts.note: made means created

indicators.note: awful rain is rain made a mess of, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moans about terrible weather, then notes it is wet indoors in the kitchen too.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags a playful definition: the wet thing in the kitchen is a liquid for soaking food.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid in which food is soaked before cooking.

clue.text: Endless anger in cheap newspaper

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Fury without end appears in a downmarket tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper, a tabloid of poor standards.

clue.text: Male bird wrecking garden

indicators.note: wrecking the word garden breaks its letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: A cock bird is tearing up the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is the male of the goose.

clue.text: Excellent facility for bride-to-be's stuff? No!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of the highest quality or class
second meaning, by contrast: a bride-to-be keeps her trousseau in the bottom drawer, so the 'No!' says it is the opposite drawer

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a bottom drawer is where a woman traditionally gathered linen and household items before marrying; the 'No!' points to the drawer at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for first-rate or upper-class, of the very best sort.

clue.text: Bill as user of letterbox?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bill is a printed notice stuck up in public
second meaning: someone who posts letters through a letterbox

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name or an invoice; here it is a placard, as in 'stick no bills'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice displayed on a wall, and one who posts mail is literally a poster.

clue.text: Place in Germany — you and I arrive on St David's Day

parts.note: you and I together are we
St David's Day, the Welsh national day, falls on 1 March, written I MAR

explanation.surface: We two reach a German town on Wales's national day.
explanation.walkthrough: St David is the patron saint of Wales; his day is 1st March, giving I (one) and MAR, the calendar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, central Germany, famed for Goethe and the Weimar Republic.

clue.text: Mum rants terribly, producing oft-repeated phrases

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of rants are thrown into a bad new order

explanation.surface: Mother complains awfully, repeating the same lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or slogan chanted or restated again and again.

clue.text: Muddle in dining-room

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a muddle or state of disorder
second meaning: a dining room for military personnel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures chaos at the dinner table; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is both a state of disorder and a place where service members eat together.

clue.text: Wee child, one locked in big building

indicators.note: locked in means held inside, so the numeral goes within the building

parts.note: a barn is a large farm building
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A little child is shut inside a huge building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' hints at the Scottish setting: bairn is Scots for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a small child.

clue.text: Busy type coming to river for drink

indicators.note: coming to means the insect arrives at the river, placed just before it

parts.note: a bee is proverbially busy, as in busy as a bee
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A busy person heads down to the river for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic beverage brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: Enchantment for a period of time?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... is a stretch of time, as in a cold ...

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a charm that lasts a while; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is both a magical incantation and a short interval, as in a spell of sunshine.

clue.text: Green leader beginning to make waves

indicators.note: waves signals that the letters move and swirl, so the pooled letters are rearranged
the beginning of make is its first letter

explanation.surface: An environmentalist party chief starts to stir things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green leader' looks like the head of the Green Party; 'Green' alone is the definition. Rearrange LEADER plus M.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green colour, named after the gemstone.
